description: Detects TypeORM @Entity() used on a domain-layer Value Object
expected_behaviors: Identifies the ORM @Entity() decorator on a domain class as a layering breach
Explains that persistence mapping does not belong in the domain layer; map it in infrastructure
Proposes a split: domain Money VO + infrastructure MoneyDAO
Provides BLOCKER severity
expectations: Runs in Review mode and produces a report with the sections Pattern(s) Detected, Layer Analysis, Findings, Recommendation
Reports the ORM @Entity() on a domain class as BLOCKER (AP-1) with the reason that persistence mapping belongs in infrastructure
Proposes a domain Money Value Object extending ValueObject plus a separate infrastructure MoneyDAO
Every finding has Evidence, Why and Fix fields
Recommendation is REDESIGN

description: Detects a Domain Service holding mutable state
expected_behaviors: Flags private result: Money as BLOCKER
Explains Node.js singleton shared state risk
Shows correct approach: return computed value instead of storing it
expectations: Flags the mutable `result: Money` field as BLOCKER (DS-1 / AP-2)
Explains that a Node.js singleton shares the field across requests
Flags `this.result = ...` as BLOCKER (AP-4) or folds it into the same finding without escalating severity
Fix returns the computed value instead of storing it on this
Recommendation is REDESIGN

expected_behaviors: Identifies Anemic Domain Model anti-pattern
Flags public mutable fields on Entity
Proposes moving the locking and balance logic into BankAccount methods
Marks as CRITICAL (a context with real business rules)
expectations: Reports the anemic BankAccount (public fields, no behavior) as CRITICAL (AP-5 / ENT-4), not BLOCKER
Reports the missing or bare primitive identity, if mentioned, as WARNING (AP-19 / ENT-1, a convention) at its own table severity
Fix moves the locking and balance logic into BankAccount methods that validate state
Fix replaces `return new Error('locked')` with a DomainBusinessError thrown from the entity
Recommendation is REFACTOR because the worst finding is CRITICAL and there is no BLOCKER

description: Approves a correctly structured Aggregate without inventing findings
expected_behaviors: Identifies CustomerAccount as Aggregate Root with global identity
Identifies BankAccount as an internal Entity with local identity (a Value Object id)
Notes private constructors with create (emits event) and restore (emits none)
Notes time and ids come from DomainDeps and the event is versioned with a static fromPrimitives
Verdict is APPROVE; no BLOCKER, CRITICAL or WARNING findings are invented
expectations: Recommendation is APPROVE
Findings contain no BLOCKER, CRITICAL or WARNING entries
At most 3 SUGGESTIONs, each tied to a rule or table row, or Findings says None
Does not ask a Grilling Loop question because the verdict is APPROVE
Does not flag the string-backed value of the id Value Objects as a bare primitive id
Does not flag aggregate size by method or entity count (AP-23 has no count trigger)

description: Implementation mode with the gate pre-answered: a single Value Object, no questions, no Turn 1 stop
input: Context: bounded context `billing`, no aggregate involved, no events. Implement an `Iban` value object that rejects malformed IBANs and exposes the country code. I already answered every question you need, just write it.
expected_behaviors: Runs in Implementation mode without asking any gate question
Skips the Turn 1 STOP because the request is a single Value Object
Iban extends ValueObject, validates through a helper called from the constructor and throws DomainValidationError
Does not ask about Domain Events and does not create any
Prints at most a short Decision Log and no checklist boxes for items that are met
expectations: The response contains code and no clarifying question
Iban extends ValueObject<string> and every field is readonly
Validation runs inside the constructor path and throws DomainValidationError, never the built-in Error
The code contains no system clock call and no ORM decorator
Any DDD Decision Log has one line per real decision; the checklist, if printed, lists only unmet or not-applicable items

description: Review in a non-interactive run: assumptions stated, full report, no blocking question

Reports the stateful field as BLOCKER and the raw Error and system clock use as WARNING
Recommendation is REDESIGN

expectations: The response contains the report sections in order and a Recommendation line
Findings are ordered BLOCKER before WARNING
The `lastOrder` field is reported as BLOCKER (DS-1) and the raw `Error` and `new Date()` at WARNING each, without escalating

description: Question mode: concept explanation gets a direct answer with no mode, no report and no gates
input: What is the difference between an Entity and an Aggregate in DDD?
expected_behaviors: Answers directly and concisely
Explains that an Entity has identity and behavior while an Aggregate is a consistency boundary around entities and value objects with one root
Does not announce a mode and does not produce a review report
Does not ask gate questions or a Grilling Loop question
expectations: The response has no '## DDD Review' heading and no Recommendation verdict
The response does not state that it is in Review or Implementation mode
The response distinguishes identity (Entity) from consistency boundary and single root (Aggregate)
The response asks no clarifying question
The response is short and does not generate a full implementation

expected_behaviors: Notes the database-assigned auto-increment id as a trade-off, not a defect

Does not flag the ORM decorator on the DAO in infrastructure
expectations: Reports the DB-assigned id (AP-18 / ENT-7) as WARNING, not CRITICAL or BLOCKER
The finding describes the trade-off (no id at creation, events and commands cannot reference it, retries cannot be deduplicated) and offers application-generated ids as the alternative
Does not report the @Entity() on InvoiceDAO as AP-1 because it lives in infrastructure
Recommendation is APPROVE or REFACTOR (at most 2 WARNINGs allows APPROVE), never REDESIGN
